subject: Cooking
title: MSG Is Not Dangerous
description: Learn MSG Is Not Dangerous in one minute.

hook.text: 'No MSG' signs hang in restaurant windows worldwide. The fear is based on a racist myth, not science.

buildup.text: In 1968, a letter to a medical journal coined 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' — blaming MSG for headaches.

discovery.text: Decades of double-blind studies have found no consistent link between MSG and any negative health effects.

twist.text: MSG occurs naturally in tomatoes, parmesan cheese, and breast milk — foods no one warns against.

climax.text: The FDA, WHO, and EU all classify MSG as safe. The scare was xenophobia dressed as science.

punchline.text: MSG is safe. The 'syndrome' was the real problem.

quiz.question: What do the FDA, WHO, and EU say about MSG safety?

details.summary: MSG (monosodium glutamate) is a safe flavor enhancer backed by decades of scientific research. The fear of MSG originated from a 1968 letter to a medical journal, not from clinical evidence. Every major food safety authority worldwide has confirmed MSG is safe for consumption.
details.whyItMatters: The MSG myth has unfairly stigmatized Asian restaurants and cuisine for decades. Recognizing MSG as safe challenges a widespread prejudice rooted in anecdote rather than science.
takeaways: WHO, FDA, and EU all classify MSG as safe for consumption
Double-blind studies found no consistent link to reported symptoms
Glutamate occurs naturally in tomatoes, parmesan, and mushrooms

faq.question: Where did the fear of MSG come from?
faq.answer: A 1968 letter in the New England Journal of Medicine described symptoms after eating Chinese food. Media amplified this into Chinese Restaurant Syndrome. Subsequent controlled studies repeatedly failed to confirm any link between MSG and the reported symptoms.

faq.question: Is MSG different from natural glutamate?
faq.answer: Chemically identical. The glutamate in MSG is the same molecule found naturally in tomatoes, parmesan cheese, soy sauce, and breast milk. Your body processes it identically regardless of source. MSG simply provides concentrated glutamate for convenient seasoning.
